column1: # _app_3c2_cvscore — CV scoring advice. Arabic spelling corrections, the AI prompt and the sample CV are internal ('-').

column2: Formatting & length
Language & spelling

A space after a punctuation mark
Repeated letters
Two spaces in a row
The file is an image or a scanned PDF — no ATS can read it, and neither can we.
Export your CV as text, not as an image
Open the original file in Word or Google Docs.
Save As → PDF (not “print to PDF” from an image).
Make sure you can select the text with the mouse inside the PDF.
The text is too short — paste the full CV or upload the file.
The email “{0}” looks unprofessional — recruiters judge how serious you are before they read.
Create an email in the firstname.lastname format
A professional email
Create an email in the firstname.lastname format on Gmail or Outlook.
Use it on your CV, on LinkedIn and when applying.
Clear email: {0}
No email — companies reach out by email first.
Add a professional email
Put the email on the second line, right under your name.
In the firstname.lastname format — no birth years or nicknames.
Valid Egyptian phone: {0}

No machine-readable phone number.
Add a phone number in a clear format
One number you actually answer, in international or local format, without symbols.
If your WhatsApp is on a different number, say so clearly.
City mentioned ({0}) — it’s used in recruiters’ filters.
State your city and governorate (not your full address).
Add your city only
City and governorate next to your contact details — no street or building.
New Cairo, Cairo
LinkedIn link present.
No LinkedIn link — 7 in 10 recruiters open it before calling.
Add a short LinkedIn link
Customise the link in LinkedIn settings so it becomes linkedin.com/in/yourname.
Make your profile headline match your CV.
Nationality
Personal details the company doesn’t need: {0} — they expose you to bias and the ATS doesn’t read them.
Remove unnecessary personal details
Remove “{0}”.
Keep: name, phone, email, city, LinkedIn — and military service status for men, because companies in Egypt ask about it.
Military service status isn’t mentioned — most companies in Egypt ask about it (for men): one line is enough.
“References available upon request” adds nothing — remove it.
A good length ({0} words).
Short ({0} words) — 3 to 5 lines is enough.
Long ({0} words) — cut it to 3–5 lines.
Adjust the summary length
3 to 5 lines: who you are, how many years, which track, what kind of projects, your strongest tool, and one achievement with a number.
States your discipline and years of experience.
The summary doesn’t clearly state your discipline and years of experience in the first line.
Open the summary with a complete introduction
First line: “[Discipline] Engineer with [N] years in [track] on [type] projects”.
Second line: your strongest tool or certification.
Third line: one achievement with a number.
Recruiters read the summary in 6 seconds and decide whether to go on.
Generic phrases or first person (looking for an opportunity, team player, I am…) — replace them with facts.
Replace generic phrases with facts
Remove “looking for an opportunity / seeking a challenging position / hard worker / works well under pressure”.
No first person — each sentence starts with the title or a verb.
Put the type and size of your projects and your strongest tool in their place.
No professional summary under your name — it’s the first thing a recruiter reads.
Add a 3–5 line professional summary under your name
Heading: “Professional Summary”.
Include: discipline, years of experience, track, type of projects, your strongest tool or certification, and one achievement with a number.
The suggested version below is written from your CV’s own details — edit it.
The summary is the first human filter; without it, your first experience bullet is read as your introduction.
Your experience is there but without a clear section heading — add a “Work Experience” heading so the ATS can find it.
{0} {0|role|roles}, all with a title, employer and dates.
{0} of {1} roles are missing {2}: “{3}”.
dates
employer
Complete every role’s header: title — company — city — from/to
First line: the exact title as in your contract.
Second line: company, city and dates in one format (Mar 2022 – Present).
Never leave a role without an end date — “Present” if it’s current.
{0} — {1} — Cairo · 03/2022 – Present
Company …
The order isn’t newest to oldest.
Order your roles from newest to oldest
Your current job first, then the earlier ones in descending order.
An average of {0} bullets per role — about right.
Too many bullets ({0} per role) — 4 to 6 for the main job, 2 to 3 for older ones.
Too few bullets ({0} per role) — 3 to 6 bullets for each main job.
Add 3–6 bullets per job
Each bullet: verb + what you did + for whom / on which project + the result as a number.
Name the project, its type and size in the first bullet.
Reviewed shop drawings for a 32,000 m² office tower and closed 180 consultant comments within 3 months.
{0} of {1} bullets start with an achievement verb.
{0}{1} bullets don’t start with an achievement verb.
bullets start with “responsible for / I did”, and
Start every bullet with an achievement verb, not a description of duties
Remove “Responsible for”, “Worked on” and “Helped”.
Start with a past-tense verb: Managed / Prepared / Reviewed / Reduced.
One bullet = verb + what + the result as a number.
Before: {0} After: {1}
Screening systems and recruiters read the first two words of every bullet.
{0} bullets with numbers (size, value, percentage, time).
Only {0} of {1} bullets contain numbers — numbers are what set your CV apart from 200 similar ones.
Add a number to every bullet you can
Project area (m²), number of floors, contract value, number of engineers or subcontractors, savings or time as a percentage.
If you don’t have an exact number, write a reasonable estimate (“about 25,000 m²”).
One number in a bullet raises the chance of a call more than any adjective.
Projects and their type are mentioned in {0} {0|role|roles} ({1}).
Most roles don’t name the project, its type and size — “Site Engineer” without a project says nothing.
Name the project in the first bullet of every job
Name or type — size or value — your role — the owner or consultant.
Capital Towers project — Administrative — 32,000 m² — Technical Office Engineer — Owner: New Urban Communities Authority
Gap of {0} — without an explanation it reads as a negative.
{0} months between “{1}” and “{2}”
Explain employment gaps in one line
One line: military service / study / freelance / travel — with dates.
Or fold the period into a freelance role if that’s what it was.
{0}{1}{2} — a bullet is one or two lines, without “I”.
bullets in the first person
long bullets (>32 words)
Shorten the bullets and drop the first person
12–25 words per bullet.
Start straight with the verb.
The summary says {0} years while the dates give ≈ {1} — make them match.
{0} {0|employer|employers} known in the EngSpace database.
No readable work experience — the most important and heaviest-weighted section of a CV.
Add an experience section that includes summer training and your graduation project
Add a “Work Experience” section with a standard heading
Heading: “Work Experience” — in exactly those words so the ATS reads it.
For every job or internship: title, company, city, dates, then 3–6 bullets that start with a verb and end with a number.

Engineering Intern — The Arab Contractors — Cairo · 07/2023 – 09/2023 - Followed the pouring of 2,400 m³ of concrete for two residential buildings and prepared daily reports approved by the site engineer.
{0} of {1} projects with a size or value.
Most projects have no size or value — “residential tower” isn’t enough.
Add the size and your role for every project
Name — type — area or value — your exact role — the owner or consultant.
Capital Gate project — Administrative — 32,000 m² — Technical Office Engineer (QS & IPCs) — Owner: New Urban Communities Authority
Make your role in every project clear.
{0} projects — pick the biggest 4–6 and the ones closest to your goal.
Projects are mentioned inside your roles — a separate section makes things clearer for the interviewer.
Add a “Key Projects” section
3 to 6 projects only — the biggest and the closest to your goal.
For each project: type, size or value, your role and the main tool.
Graduation project mentioned — the most important item for fresh graduates.
No graduation project and no training projects — in engineering, that’s what interviewers ask about first.
No projects section — in engineering, that’s what interviewers ask about first.
Add your graduation project in detail
Project name and type, your role in the team, the tool (Revit/ETABS…), and the grade or result.
3 to 6 projects — the biggest and the closest to your goal.
Graduation project: design of a 15-storey residential tower — structural analysis and design in ETABS and SAFE — grade: Excellent
The degree or department isn’t clear — “B.Sc. in … Engineering”.
State your degree and department explicitly
“B.Sc. in Civil Engineering” — in exactly those words so the ATS matches it.
Give the full names of the university and faculty.
Graduation year not mentioned — it’s used to estimate experience.
Add your graduation year
One year is enough (2019) — or the period (2014 – 2019).
Grade mentioned — after 5 years’ experience you can drop it unless it’s Excellent.
Grade not mentioned — most companies ask about it for under 3 years’ experience (include it if it’s Good or higher).
Add your overall grade
Very Good / Excellent / GPA — if it’s Good or higher; otherwise leave it out.
Fresh graduates: add your graduation project (name, tool, your role, grade).
Education has no separate section heading — add “Education”.
No readable qualification.
Add an “Education” section
Education: degree, department, faculty, university, graduation year, and grade if it’s Good or higher.
B.Sc. in Civil Engineering — Cairo University · 2021 · Grade: Very Good
Education before experience — after your first two years of experience, experience comes first.
Fresh graduates: put education before experience.
Skills section ({0} known {0|tool|tools} in it).
No separate skills section — the ATS looks for keywords there first.
Add a “Skills & Software” section with the exact tool names
Heading: Skills.
Write each tool’s commercial name: AutoCAD, Revit, ETABS — not “design software”.
Group them: software · codes & standards · management.

Group your skills (software / codes / management) instead of one long list.

Name them exactly in your skills section and in at least one experience bullet — the ATS counts repetition.

Screening systems match the ad’s words literally; a tool not written by name doesn’t count.
All the core keywords for your track are present.
Codes & standards: {0}.
No codes or standards (ECP, ACI, ASHRAE, NFPA, IEC…) — they set an engineer apart from a draughtsman.

Cut down generic soft skills
Keep one or two with examples, and remove the rest.
Soft skills are proven in your experience bullets, not in a list.
Rating bars, stars or percentages for skills — the ATS can’t read them and they look subjective.
Replace rating bars with words
Advanced / Working knowledge — or just name the tool.
The tool list is too long — 10 to 15 tools, most important first.

No certifications or courses — even a short course in a tool counts.

Course, provider, year — newest first.

Engineers Syndicate membership mentioned.
Engineers Syndicate membership isn’t mentioned — it’s required to practise in Egypt, and one line proves it.
Languages with a clear level: {0}.
Give the level of each language (Very good / Fluent / B2).
No languages — English is required at consultancies and international firms.
Add your languages with their level
Arabic: native · English: Very good (B2) — and mention IELTS/TOEFL if you have it.
Short ({0} words) — add detail to your experience and projects.

{0} different bullet styles — use one.
Mixed date formats (03/2022, Jan 2022 and 2022) — one format across the whole CV.
Use one date format
Mar 2022 – Present or 03/2022 – Present — just one.
Many lines in full capitals — hard to read.
Two-column layout — most ATS read it scrambled and mix up the sections.
{0} {0|table|tables} in the file — tables are read row by row and get mixed up in the ATS.

One style of numerals across the whole CV
Arabic and English in one sentence

Each heading on its own line in a slightly heavier weight — no icons or columns.
The ATS looks for these words to know where to read your experience and where to read your education.
Switch the design to one column with no tables
Columns and tables are read scrambled in the ATS.
A simple template: headings, then bullets, top to bottom.
Remove the personal photo and icons
A photo isn’t required in Egypt and confuses automatic screening — unless the company explicitly asks for one.
